title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 112 (Representation of President and Governors in meetings)

content.overview: Section 112(1) provides that the President of India or the Governor of a State, if a member of a company, may appoint such person as he thinks fit to act as his representative at any meeting of the company or of any class of members. Section 112(2) deems that person a member for the purposes of the Act and entitles him to exercise the same rights and powers, including the right to vote by proxy and postal ballot, as the President or Governor could exercise as a member.
content.glance: The President or a State Governor who is a member may appoint a representative to attend and exercise membership rights (including proxy and postal ballot) at company or class meetings.
content.study:
## Section 112 — representation of President and Governors

**Subsection (1): power to appoint.** The President of India or the Governor of a State, if he is a member of a company, may appoint such person as he thinks fit to act as his representative at any meeting of the company or at any meeting of any class of members of the company.

**Subsection (2): status and rights.** A person appointed under subsection (1) shall, for the purposes of this Act, be deemed to be a member of such a company and shall be entitled to exercise the same rights and powers, including the right to vote by proxy and postal ballot, as the President or, as the case may be, the Governor could exercise as a member of the company.

## Apply the provision
- Confirm that the President or Governor is a member of the company.
- Identify the appointment of the representative for a company meeting or class meeting.
- The representative is deemed a member and may vote by proxy and postal ballot to the same extent as the appointing authority could.

Distinguish from section 113 (representation of body corporates by board/governing-body resolution). This note is a focused study aid; the topic remains under source and current-law review.

provisions.title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 112 (Representation of President and Governors in meetings)

examples.title: Governor's representative at a class meeting
examples.body: The Governor of a State is a member of a company and appoints a person to act as representative at a meeting of a class of members. Under section 112 that person is deemed a member and may exercise the same rights, including proxy and postal ballot, as the Governor could. This is an educational illustration.

hypotheticals.question: Can a person appointed under section 112 vote by postal ballot?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. Subsection (2) expressly includes the right to vote by proxy and postal ballot among the rights the representative may exercise as the President or Governor could as a member.

distinctions.title: Section 112 compared with section 113
distinctions.left: Section 112 — President or Governor as member appoints a representative
distinctions.right: Section 113 — body corporate (member or creditor) authorises a representative by board/governing-body resolution

rows.right: Board of Directors or other governing body of the body corporate

misconceptions.trap: Treating section 112 as applying to any public authority or government department as member.
misconceptions.correction: Section 112 is limited to the President of India or the Governor of a State when that office-holder is a member.

misconceptions.trap: Confusing section 112 with section 113 body-corporate representation.
misconceptions.correction: Section 112 is specific to the President/Governor; section 113 covers body corporates authorising representatives by board or governing-body resolution.
